The strongest faithful repair preserves field scope, but leaves score lifting open. Chen–Santos gives the right proof architecture, not a theorem that applies under the current continuity-only assumptions: its local nuisance-space and density conditions are essentially the missing incidence/path-realization work here. Treating \((h,q)\) as a product nuisance is legitimate, but finite-rank constraint moments apply only to the finite-support germs.

The claimed equivalence “pathwise differentiable iff \(\Phi_P\neq\varnothing\)” is unsupported under bridge existence plus separate \(L^2\) assumptions. Replace it by a one-way sufficient theorem and isolate necessity as a separate representer obligation.

Use these directives separately.

--require-core-target oeq:score-lifting-completeness

Attempt a Chen–Santos-style proof only after verifying its local-parameter hypotheses for this model. Write the coupled nuisance as eta=(h_0,h_1,q_0,q_1) and the incidence map as the two outcome residual maps g_a-T_a h_a and the two adjoint residual maps 1-T_a^*q_a, coupled through the common observed law and shared (W,X) marginal. Quotient nuisance derivatives by the outcome and treatment kernels.

Audit, rather than assume, the analogues of Chen–Santos Assumption 4.1(iv) and (v): prove that the declared product nuisance perturbations are genuinely attainable in a local chart of the nonlinear incidence set, and prove that bounded feasible directions are dense in the relevant annihilator. Only after those facts are derived may Chen–Santos Theorem 4.1 be used to identify the normal and tangent orthocomplement. Operator continuity and continuous kernel projections are insufficient because they provide neither a differentiable incidence chart nor local surjectivity.

Do not append “Chen–Santos regularity,” “local richness,” a split-submersion premise, or density of attainable scores as a new assumption and then mark the OEQ solved; those are the present crux. Finite rank/Schur constraint moments may be added to the product moment map only on the already certified finite-support germs. The unrestricted fixed-defect Hilbert stratum is not described by finitely many such moments.

If Assumptions 4.1(iv)–(v) cannot be proved from the frozen saturated-chart primitives, leave this OEQ open and record the exact failed range/local-parameter step. A valid resolution must either construct the actual DQM paths or exhibit a counterexample within the full saturated germ, not within an analyst-selected subchart.

Adaptation source: Chen–Santos (2018), Definition 2.1 for DQM paths; Assumptions 4.1(iv)–(v) and their discussion for the local nuisance space and bounded-direction density; Theorem 4.1 for the derivative-range/normal-space conclusion.

--require-core-target thm:quotient-efficiency

Remove the unsupported assertion that theta is pathwise differentiable if and only if Phi_P is nonempty under mere bridge existence and separate L2 integrability.

Replace it by the strongest sound one-way theorem. At P, suppose:
(1) the actual tangent equality T_P=C_P^perp has been proved;
(2) there is a base bridge pair (h,q) whose score phi_{h,q} lies in L_0^2(P);
(3) for every admissible DQM path there are nearby bridge representatives for which the exact primal-dual mixed-bias remainder is o(t), with the linear score term uniformly integrable. A sufficient quantitative form is
  min{||T_a(h_{a,t}-h_a)||_2 ||q_{a,t}-q_a||_2,
      ||h_{a,t}-h_a||_2 ||T_a^*(q_{a,t}-q_a)||_2}=o(|t|)
for each arm, together with the product-envelope condition needed for the DQM inner-product limit.

Prove from the exact mixed-bias identity that phi_{h,q} represents every actual path derivative. Then the already-proved affine identity and Hilbert projection give
  A_P=phi_0+C_P,
  phi_eff=phi_0-Pi_{C_P}phi_0,
  V_eff=inf_{phi in A_P} E phi^2.
Do not assume “bridge-score pathwise validity” under a renamed condition without proving it from the displayed product remainder and DQM integrability.

State necessity separately. Pathwise differentiability alone gives a continuous Riesz representer on the actual tangent space. It does not currently imply that a gradient is an individual square-integrable bridge-pair score. If a rich bounded-outcome-tilt submodel can be constructed, derive the corresponding adjoint-range/Riesz necessity; leave the further implication Phi_P nonempty as an open representer/product-integrability obligation unless proved. Do not retain an iff frontier based only on existence and L2 bridges.

Adaptation source: Bennett et al., arXiv:2307.13793, pp. 1–4, for the exact mixed-bias identity and the sufficient product condition using the minimum of primal-residual×dual-error and primal-error×adjoint-residual.

--require-core-target lem:learned-projection-convergence

Replace the same-training-sample ridge construction by nested three-way cross-fitting. For each evaluation fold I_k, split its complement into disjoint construction and calibration samples A_k and C_k, each of order n. Learn all bridge representatives and dictionary functions only on A_k. Conditional on A_k, evaluate that fixed learned dictionary on C_k to form the calibration Gram and score cross-moment, compute the projection coefficients there, and evaluate the resulting signal only on I_k. Foldwise coefficients, dictionaries, weights, and signals must carry (-k) and construction/calibration labels.

Use the exact cell expansion
  S(hhat,qhat)-S(h0,q0)
  =(1-Iq0)(hhat-h0)+I(Y-h0)(qhat-q0)-I(qhat-q0)(hhat-h0).
Introduce explicit L4 multiplier envelopes for 1-Iq0 and I(Y-h0). If d_{j,n} bounds coordinate j, define
  delta_D,n=(sum_{j<=J_n} d_{j,n}^2)^{1/2},
and show delta_D,n<=sqrt(J_n) max_j d_{j,n}; do not use a dimension-free dictionary rate.

Conditional on A_k, derive calibration concentration from declared bounded/sub-Gaussian or sufficiently high-moment envelopes. A valid representative rate is
  eta_G,n = O_p[B_D,n^2{sqrt(J_n log J_n/n_C)+J_n log J_n/n_C}],
  eta_c,n = O_p[B_D,n B_0,n sqrt(J_n log J_n/n_C)],
with the precise envelope convention stated. Do not attribute this concentration to evaluation-fold independence.

Handle singular population Grams explicitly. Prefer a calibration spectral cutoff: project onto empirical eigenvalues above tau_n and ridge only there, with population positive eigenvalue kappa_J, eta_G,n+dictionary-perturbation=o(tau_n), tau_n<kappa_J/2 eventually, and rho_n=o(kappa_J). Alternatively prove explicit population-null-space leakage bounds at scale o(rho_n); ordinary full-space ridge alone is insufficient.

Carry coefficient factors through the resolvent. A sufficient prediction bound must have the form
  alpha_J
  +L_n delta_D,n
  +(sqrt(Lambda_J)/kappa_J){eta_c,n+(eta_G,n+rho_n)L_n}
  +spectral-projector error
  =o_p(1),
where L_n controls both the affine-weight envelope and the learned coefficient norm. Include rho_n||b_J||/kappa_J and eta_G,n||bhat||/kappa_J rather than dropping those factors. Prove the coefficient-to-affine-weight identity and then derive learned efficient-signal convergence; never assume that convergence.

Adaptation sources: DML arXiv:1608.00060, §3.2, for cross-fitted nuisance/evaluation separation; Bennett et al., arXiv:2307.13793, pp. 1–4, for the bridge mixed-bias decomposition. The independent calibration layer and spectral-cutoff repair are additional constructions required here because standard DML does not justify a Gram evaluated on the dictionary-training sample.

--require-core-target thm:affine-ensemble-inference
